answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a costly, slow-maturing stake that cannot be split across copies. Like a yarrow root that only grips after seasons of growth, the stake is earned through verifiable work history, not bought in an instant. A river of small signed attestations from real trading partners flows into a public ledger, so a fresh identity with no history is a lone pearl in an empty shell: pretty, but untrusted. Copying an identity transfers no stake and no history, so forging a thousand agents costs a thousand real deposits.
